title: Wavy Walls May Help Homes Stand Up to Hurricane Winds
summary:
Engineers in Florida tested a cool idea for storm safety: give walls and roofs gentle waves instead of flat sides.

They 3D-printed small building models. Some were flat. Others had waves of different sizes. In a wind tunnel, the wavy models felt less wind force. The deepest waves cut peak pressure near corners by about 40 to 60 percent. Corners are where wind often does the most damage.

On a flat roof, wind can make one big swirl that sucks upward, almost like peeling a sticker. On a wavy surface, the air skips along and makes many smaller swirls, so the strong suction is weaker.

Pedro Fernández-Cabán, a civil engineer at Florida State University, said unusual shapes can reduce damage in severe weather. The team still needs more tests. If the idea works on real houses, wavy designs could help communities that face strong storms.
why_it_matters: Strong storms can hurt homes; smarter shapes could help keep families safer.
